13	  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
14	  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
15	  source: donetick
16	quirks:
17	  - "⛔⛔ THE CONTAINER REFUSES TO START UNTIL YOU SET DT_JWT_SECRET, AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT WOULD OTHERWISE EAT YOUR EVENING. Dockerfile:43 copies the repo's config directory INTO the image, so /config/selfhosted.yaml ships with jwt.secret set to the placeholder string change_this_to_a_secure_random_string_32_characters_long. config/config.go:404-446 puts that exact string in a weakSecrets list and PANICS the process when it matches, or when the secret is shorter than 32 characters. The log prints a SECURITY ERROR block, suggests a generated secret, and aborts. So a deploy that passes no environment at all produces a crash-looping container and a redu build that never goes healthy, and the cause is a config file you never wrote. Generate 32 or more random alphanumeric characters and pass DT_JWT_SECRET. This is fail-loud rather than fail-silent, which is the good version of this trap, but only if you know why."
18	  - "PASS THE SAME DT_JWT_SECRET ON EVERY REDEPLOY. It signs every session token (jwt.session_time defaults to 168h in the shipped config, max_refresh 1440h), so a new value on each deploy silently logs every user out, including the mobile app and any long-lived API token flow that rides on it. Nothing errors. Generate it ONCE, hand it to the user, and reuse it forever. It is not a database key, so rotating it destroys no data; it destroys sessions."
19	  - "⛔⛔ DATABASE: SET DT_DATABASE_TYPE=postgres EXACTLY, BECAUSE ANYTHING ELSE SILENTLY MEANS SQLITE. internal/database/database.go:59-77 is a switch with ONE case, \"postgres\", and a default branch that opens SQLite. A typo, the string postgresql, or an override that did not take all land in the default branch, so the app comes up perfectly healthy, serves the UI, saves your chores, and loses all of them at the next VM replacement (the file is $DT_SQLITE_PATH, or ./donetick.db relative to /, when that is unset). Set ALL of: DT_DATABASE_TYPE=postgres, DT_DATABASE_HOST=${PGHOST}, DT_DATABASE_PORT=${PGPORT}, DT_DATABASE_USER=${PGUSER}, DT_DATABASE_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value]}, DT_DATABASE_NAME=${PGDATABASE}. deploy_compose with database:'managed' only APPENDS those PG variables to the project .env; it never edits your compose, so the compose has to interpolate them itself. Environment variables beat the baked config file: config/config.go:350-352 sets the DT prefix and replaces dots with underscores, then AutomaticEnv applies them over the file."
20	  - "⛔ PROVE WHICH DATABASE IT LANDED IN, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BECAUSE A GREEN PAGE PROVES NOTHING HERE. POSITIVE, and run it first because it also proves your exec command works at all: `sudo docker exec <container> printenv DT_DATABASE_TYPE DT_DATABASE_HOST` must print postgres and the managed private IP. POSITIVE, and this is the one that settles it: connect to the managed Postgres and confirm Donetick's tables are there (the migrations create users, circles and chores among others, and the startup log prints 'Applied N migrations!'). NEGATIVE, and only meaningful next to those two: `sudo docker exec <container> ls -la /donetick.db` should not find a file. The runtime image is alpine, so it has a shell and exec really works, unlike the distroless entries elsewhere in this library."
21	  - "THE POSTGRES CONNECTION IS UNENCRYPTED AND YOU CANNOT CHANGE IT FROM CONFIG. internal/database/database.go:61 builds the DSN with sslmode=disable and TimeZone=Asia/Shanghai written into the format string, with no configuration hook for either. Over redu's private network, where the managed database VM is not reachable from the internet, plaintext is survivable, and it is still worth saying out loud at handover rather than letting the user assume TLS. The hardcoded time zone applies to the database session; set the container's own TZ variable for the application's clock, which is what drives due dates and the scheduler."
22	  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: NOBODY, AND THAT IS AN UNUSUAL ANSWER WORTH READING TWICE. Donetick has no instance administrator and no first-user privilege. internal/user/handler.go:175-195: every account that signs up gets its OWN circle (its household) and is given the admin role INSIDE THAT CIRCLE ONLY. A stranger who signs up on your instance therefore cannot see your chores, but they do get an account, a circle, storage and scheduler work on the VM you are paying for, and there is no admin UI anywhere to remove them: deleting them means SQL against the managed database. The ONLY instance-level control is closing signups, described next. The dashboard-view and admin/manager roles named in the README are also circle roles, resolved from OIDC groups (internal/auth/role_resolver.go), not instance roles."
23	  - "⛔ CLOSE SIGNUPS, AND DO IT AFTER YOU HAVE CREATED YOUR OWN ACCOUNT. The shipped config has is_user_creation_disabled: false, so registration is open to anyone the moment the hostname resolves. Two switches do the same thing: DT_IS_USER_CREATION_DISABLED=true through the normal viper path, and DONETICK_DISABLE_SIGNUP=true, which is the ONE variable in this app that does NOT use the DT_ prefix (config/config.go:317). Set it and internal/user/handler.go:115-120 answers 403 'User creation is disabled' to POST /api/v1/auth/ before it even parses the body. Order matters: create the household's accounts first, then close the door and redeploy. There is no invite system to let people in afterwards, so reopening means another redeploy."
24	  - "⛔ DT_SINGLE_CIRCLE_INSTANCE=true CHANGES WHO LANDS IN YOUR HOUSEHOLD. It hides the circle-management UI and puts new OIDC users into the SHARED circle (ID 1) instead of giving them their own, which is what makes a family instance pleasant. It also means that anyone your identity provider lets in is inside your task list rather than beside it. Only enable it together with an identity provider whose membership you control, and pair it with DT_DISABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH=[REDACTED:value] so password signup is not a second, ungoverned door."
25	  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH: the frontend, GET /health (which returns status, version and commit, internal/resource/handler.go:53-63), GET /api/v1/health (bodyless 200, main.go:341-343), and GET /api/v1/resource, which is unauthenticated and reports is_user_creation_disabled, single_circle_instance, disable_password_auth, the API version and the configured OIDC client id and auth URL. That last one is genuinely useful for verification and it is also a fingerprint, so treat the version it publishes as public information. Everything else is behind the JWT middleware. The shipped config also has serve_swagger true, which publishes the API documentation at /swagger/index.html: harmless, and set server.serve_swagger false if the user would rather not advertise the surface."
26	  - "⛔ PIN donetick/donetick:v0.1.76 WITH THE v, AND KNOW WHAT THE RELEASE FEED LOOKS LIKE. Measured against the Docker Hub API on 2026-08-17: the v0.1.76 tag exists (pushed 2026-07-26) and the same version WITHOUT the v returns 404. v0.1.76 is the newest NON-prerelease release; the five newest GitHub releases are all betas, and a rolling `beta` tag on Docker Hub tracks them. This project ships beta tags frequently, so pinning matters more here than usual: take the newest stable tag deliberately rather than following latest."
27	  - "⛔ DO NOT ADAPT THE REPO'S docker-compose.yaml. It is wrong for the published image in three separate ways: it builds from the Dockerfile instead of pulling, it publishes 8085:8000 when the server listens on 2021 (config/selfhosted.yaml:22, Dockerfile:50), and it overrides the command with /donetick-core, which does not exist in the image (Dockerfile:33 and :42 build and copy /donetick). Copy the compose from the README instead, which is correct, then drop its SQLite volume and DT_SQLITE_PATH once the managed Postgres is wired."
28	  - "PORT 2021, AND THERE ARE TWO HEALTH ENDPOINTS WITH DIFFERENT BODIES. Pass 2021 to deploy_compose. Dockerfile:52-53 defines a container HEALTHCHECK using wget against /health, which the alpine image has (there is no curl in it, so a curl-based healthcheck silently never succeeds). For your own probing prefer GET /health, because it returns a JSON body with status, version and commit and can therefore prove you are talking to Donetick, while /api/v1/health returns a bare 200 that an error page could imitate."
29	  - "SET DT_SERVER_PUBLIC_HOST TO THE REAL HTTPS URL. It defaults to http://localhost:2021 (config/config.go:137) and it feeds generated links, including the Swagger host and the password-reset URL. Generate the dname yourself in full `donetick-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so the value is known before the container starts, and set it as https://<that>, with no trailing slash. If the user will also use the mobile app or any other cross-origin client, the shipped cors_allow_origins list contains only localhost entries, and it is a list, so it is easier to override by mounting your own selfhosted.yaml than through the environment."
30	  - "NO SMTP MEANS NO PASSWORD RESET BY EMAIL, AND THE SHIPPED CONFIG SAYS SO. The email block in config/selfhosted.yaml is empty and carries log_raw_url: true, which logs the password-reset URL to the console when mail is not configured. So a lost password on a fresh instance is recovered by reading the container log, which is fine for a household and worth stating at handover. Point the email block at a relay the user already owns if they want real resets, and remember the app also speaks Telegram, Discord and Pushover for notifications, none of which needs SMTP."
31	  - "PHOTO ATTACHMENTS DEFAULT TO S3, NOT TO LOCAL DISK, WHICH SURPRISES PEOPLE. internal/storage/factory.go:10-17: storage_type \"local\" uses the filesystem and ANYTHING else, including the empty default in the shipped config, constructs an S3 client. Building it does not fail with empty credentials, so the app starts happily and the problem only appears when somebody attaches a photo. If the user wants photos: either set the storage block to local with a base_path inside a mounted volume, or give it real S3-compatible credentials (bucket, region, endpoint, access key, secret key). If they do not, nothing is broken, that feature is simply unused."
32	  - "NO VOLUME IS NEEDED ONCE POSTGRES IS WIRED, WITH ONE EXCEPTION. Chores, circles, users and history all live in the managed database. The /donetick-data volume in upstream's compose exists only for the SQLite file this recipe deliberately does not use, so mounting it and assuming it protects something is a mistake. The exception is local photo storage: if you enable it, mount a volume and put the base_path inside it, and say plainly that those files live on the app VM and go with it."
33	  - "NO migrate_command. config/selfhosted.yaml:10 sets database.migration true and main.go:279-280 runs the migrations at startup, printing 'Applied N migrations!'. A fresh managed Postgres is therefore populated on first boot and an upgrade applies its own migrations. Donetick needs exactly ONE database and creates no second one, so redu's one-database-per-managed-server rule never bites, and no db_superuser is needed."
34	  - "SIZING IS REASONING, NOT A MEASUREMENT. Upstream publishes no memory figure anywhere (checked README, Dockerfile, their compose and the shipped config). m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB) is chosen because this is one statically linked Go binary with the frontend embedded in it, running on alpine, with the database on a separate VM. The scheduler jobs (due, overdue and pre-due, every 30m to 3h in the shipped config) and the realtime SSE service (1000 connections allowed by default) are the only background load. ---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/donetick/donetick
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: donetick/donetick:v0.1.76
  port: 2021
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0348
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: donetick
quirks:
  - "THE CONTAINER REFUSES TO START UNTIL YOU SET DT_JWT_SECRET. Dockerfile:43 copies the repo's config directory INTO the image, so /config/selfhosted.yaml ships with jwt.secret set to the placeholder string change_this_to_a_secure_random_string_32_characters_long. config/config.go:404-446 puts that exact string in a weakSecrets list and PANICS the process when it matches, or when the secret is shorter than 32 characters."
  - "PASS THE SAME DT_JWT_SECRET ON EVERY REDEPLOY. It signs every session token (jwt.session_time defaults to 168h, max_refresh 1440h), so a new value on each deploy silently logs every user out."
  - "DATABASE: SET DT_DATABASE_TYPE=postgres EXACTLY, BECAUSE ANYTHING ELSE SILENTLY MEANS SQLITE. internal/database/database.go:59-77 is a switch with ONE case, postgres, and a default branch that opens SQLite. Set ALL of: DT_DATABASE_TYPE, DT_DATABASE_HOST=${PGHOST}, DT_DATABASE_PORT=${PGPORT}, DT_DATABASE_USER=${PGUSER}, DT_DATABASE_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value]}, DT_DATABASE_NAME=${PGDATABASE}. deploy_compose with database:'managed' only APPENDS those PG variables to the project .env; the compose has to interpolate them itself."
  - "PROVE WHICH DATABASE IT LANDED IN, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. sudo docker exec <container> printenv DT_DATABASE_TYPE DT_DATABASE_HOST must print postgres and the managed private IP; Donetick's tables must exist in the managed Postgres; sudo docker exec <container> ls -la /donetick.db should not find a file. The runtime image is alpine, so exec really works."
  - "THE POSTGRES CONNECTION IS UNENCRYPTED AND YOU CANNOT CHANGE IT FROM CONFIG. internal/database/database.go:61 builds the DSN with sslmode=disable and TimeZone=Asia/Shanghai in the format string. Set the container's own TZ variable for the application's clock."
  - "WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: NOBODY. Donetick has no instance administrator and no first-user privilege. internal/user/handler.go:175-195: every account that signs up gets its OWN circle and is admin INSIDE THAT CIRCLE ONLY. There is no admin UI to remove them."
  - "CLOSE SIGNUPS AFTER YOU HAVE CREATED YOUR OWN ACCOUNT. Shipped config has is_user_creation_disabled: false. Two switches: DT_IS_USER_CREATION_DISABLED=true and DONETICK_DISABLE_SIGNUP=true, which is the ONE variable that does NOT use the DT_ prefix (config/config.go:317)."
  - "DT_SINGLE_CIRCLE_INSTANCE=true CHANGES WHO LANDS IN YOUR HOUSEHOLD. Only enable it with an identity provider whose membership you control, paired with DT_DISABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH=[REDACTED:value]"
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH: the frontend, GET /health (status, version, commit), GET /api/v1/health (bodyless 200), and GET /api/v1/resource (is_user_creation_disabled, single_circle_instance, disable_password_auth, API version, OIDC client id and auth URL). serve_swagger is true by default."
  - "PIN donetick/donetick:v0.1.76 WITH THE v. Measured against the Docker Hub API on 2026-08-17: the v0.1.76 tag exists (pushed 2026-07-26) and the same version WITHOUT the v returns 404. v0.1.76 is the newest NON-prerelease release; a rolling beta tag tracks the betas."
  - "DO NOT ADAPT THE REPO'S docker-compose.yaml. It builds from the Dockerfile instead of pulling, publishes 8085:8000 when the server listens on 2021, and overrides the command with /donetick-core, which does not exist in the image. Copy the compose from the README instead, then drop its SQLite volume and DT_SQLITE_PATH."
  - "PORT 2021, AND THERE ARE TWO HEALTH ENDPOINTS WITH DIFFERENT BODIES. Dockerfile:52-53 defines a HEALTHCHECK using wget against /health (no curl in the alpine image). Prefer GET /health for probing because it returns JSON with status, version and commit."
  - "SET DT_SERVER_PUBLIC_HOST TO THE REAL HTTPS URL. It defaults to http://localhost:2021 (config/config.go:137) and feeds generated links, including the Swagger host and the password-reset URL. Generate the dname yourself in full donetick-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form."
  - "NO SMTP MEANS NO PASSWORD RESET BY EMAIL. The email block in config/selfhosted.yaml is empty and carries log_raw_url: true, which logs the password-reset URL to the console."
  - "PHOTO ATTACHMENTS DEFAULT TO S3, NOT TO LOCAL DISK. internal/storage/factory.go:10-17: storage_type local uses the filesystem and ANYTHING else, including the empty default, constructs an S3 client."
  - "NO VOLUME IS NEEDED ONCE POSTGRES IS WIRED, WITH ONE EXCEPTION: local photo storage."
  - "NO migrate_command. config/selfhosted.yaml:10 sets database.migration true and main.go:279-280 runs the migrations at startup, printing 'Applied N migrations!'. Donetick needs exactly ONE database, so redu's one-database-per-managed-server rule never bites, and no db_superuser is needed."
  - "SIZING IS REASONING, NOT A MEASUREMENT. Upstream publishes no memory figure. m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB) is chosen because this is one statically linked Go binary with the frontend embedded, on alpine, with the database on a separate VM."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> generate the dname and a 32+ character JWT secret up front -> plan_deploy -> show the user the plan and the cost and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '2' (m1.small), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2', port 2021 -> create the household's accounts -> then redeploy with signups disabled."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# HOST=donetick-5nyvi89p.redu.cloud ./verify.sh
set -u
: "${HOST:?set HOST to the public hostname}"

body=$(mktemp)
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/health")

if [ "$code" = "502" ] || [ "$code" = "503" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: the edge answered $code, which is what redu serves while a container is"
  echo "still starting. It is also what you get from a container that is crash-looping on a weak"
  echo "JWT secret, so if this persists, read the container log before re-running."
  rm -f "$body"; exit 2
fi
[ "$code" = "200" ] || { echo "FAIL: /health answered $code"; rm -f "$body"; exit 1; }

# Positive control FIRST: Donetick's own health document.
grep -q '"status":"healthy"' "$body" || {
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: HTTP 200 but the body is not Donetick's health JSON."
  rm -f "$body"; exit 2; }
echo "OK: /health is Donetick's own health document:"; cat "$body"; echo
rm -f "$body"

flag=$(curl -sSL "https://$HOST/api/v1/resource")
echo "$flag" | grep -q 'is_user_creation_disabled' || {
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/v1/resource did not answer with the expected fields."; exit 2; }

# TEST THE BEHAVIOUR, not the flag. Empty body -> 400 when signup is open, 403 before the body
# is parsed when it is closed. Probes the door without creating an account.
sig=$(printf '{}' | curl -sSL -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
        -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- \
        "https://$HOST/api/v1/auth/")
case "$sig" in
  403) echo "OK: signup is CLOSED (403 before the body is parsed)" ;;
  400) echo "NOTE: signup is OPEN. Anyone with this URL can create an account and their own"
       echo "circle. Expected while you are still creating the household's accounts; set"
       echo "DONETICK_DISABLE_SIGNUP=true and redeploy once you are done." ;;
  404) echo "INCONCLUSIVE: the signup route answered 404, so it has moved and this check proves"
       echo "nothing. Find the current route before trusting anything here."; exit 2 ;;
  *)   echo "INCONCLUSIVE: signup probe answered $sig, which is neither 400 nor 403."; exit 2 ;;
esac

echo
echo "Still to confirm, and it cannot be seen from out here: WHICH database."
echo "  sudo docker exec <container> printenv DT_DATABASE_TYPE DT_DATABASE_HOST"
echo "  must print postgres and the managed private IP, and Donetick's tables must exist in"
echo "  the managed Postgres. A healthy page proves nothing about that."
